content:
Ask any Class 7 Olympiad topper which chapter they refuse to lose marks in, and Integers comes up first. The questions look easy — and that is exactly the trap. Take the free IMO Class 7 Integers online test below. It has 10 Olympiad-pattern MCQs with instant scoring. Every answer comes with a worked explanation. Aim for 8 out of 10.

What the IMO asks from Integers in Class 7

  • Ordering, comparing and absolute value.
  • All four operations with negative numbers.
  • Properties: closure, commutativity, distributivity.
  • Number-line journeys, temperatures, depths and money.
  • Multi-step puzzles: magic squares, digit games.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • (−) × (−) = (+), and (−) × (+) = (−) — sign first, digits second.
  • Subtracting an integer means adding its opposite: a − (−b) = a + b.
  • |−7| = 7: absolute value is distance from zero, never negative.
  • Division by zero is undefined — 0 ÷ 5 = 0, but 5 ÷ 0 does not exist.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Computing −3² as 9 (it is −9 unless the minus is inside the bracket).
  • Jumping the wrong way on the number line for subtraction.
  • Forgetting that the sum of an integer and its opposite is 0, not the number itself.

quiz.title: IMO Class 7 Integers Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an integer?
questions.explanation: An integer is any number from the set {…, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3, …}. 0, −3 and 100 all belong to this set. 5/2 = 2.5 is a rational number, not an integer.

questions.q: What is the absolute difference between the largest negative integer and the smallest positive integer?
questions.explanation: The largest negative integer is −1 and the smallest positive integer is 1. |(−1) − 1| = |−2| = 2.

questions.q: Which of the following operations on the set of integers does NOT possess the closure property?
questions.explanation: Adding, subtracting or multiplying two integers always produces an integer. Division can leave the set: 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5 is not an integer. So integers are not closed under division.
Take out the common factor −85 (distributive property). (−85) × (98 + 2) = (−85) × 100 = −8500.

questions.q: At midnight the temperature was −8°C. By 6 AM it rose by 5°C. By noon it fell by 9°C. What was the temperature at noon?
In an exam, +4 marks are given per correct answer, −2 per incorrect answer, and 0 for unattempted questions. Rohan answers 18 correctly and 7 incorrectly. What is his total score?
If a * b = a + b − ab, evaluate (−3) * 4.
The product of three consecutive integers is −504. What is their sum?
questions.explanation: 8³ = 512 is close to 504, and the product is negative. Test (−9) × (−8) × (−7) = −504. It works. Sum = −9 − 8 − 7 = −24.
